props.name: zinc-chromium binary methanol synthesis catalyst (Fauser converter)
props.note: composition, chemical form and supplier not stated

props.name: feed CO2 converted to methanol under the same conditions
props.statement: The 4-5% CO2 in the synthesis feed is not removed: CO2 + 3H2 = CH3OH + H2O forms methanol under almost the same conditions as CO, only consuming 1 mol more H2 and slightly increasing the water in crude methanol; synthesizing with this much CO2 was judged economical.

props.name: CO2 and O2 in concentrate harmless
props.statement: The CO2 in the concentrated gas saves CO2 make-up in reforming and its O2 amounts to a slight partial oxidation that reduces reformer fuel, so neither causes trouble.

props.name: crude methanol composition
props.statement: Crude methanol from the converter contains about 12% water, 1.8% light ends (mainly dimethyl ether) and about 0.8% heavy ends (mainly isobutanol), the rest methanol.

props.name: Fauser converter cooling by water coils
props.note: the coil water pressure is 50 kg/cm2 in this plant versus 300 kg/cm2 in the former Fauser type; the purpose is the author's surmise ('思われる')
props.statement: The Fauser process removes reaction heat by natural circulation of water in cooling coils separate from the gas circuit and recovers it as steam, whereas other processes control temperature by the recycle gas rate or cold-gas injection between beds; in this plant the coil water is at 50 kg/cm2 instead of the 300 kg/cm2 of the former Fauser type, which seems to aim at a larger cooling capacity and easier circulation, with a simpler coil system.

props.name: cryogenic unit free of explosion hazard
props.statement: Compression to about 5 atm and 150 °C (all-low-pressure cycle), leaving 30% methane in the waste gas, and removing CO2 in large regenerators were confirmed to exclude any explosion hazard in the methane concentration unit.

props.name: methane formation above 400 °C causes runaway
props.statement: Temperature control of the methanol catalyst bed is much more difficult than for ammonia: above 400 °C the methane-forming reaction starts abruptly and its large heat of reaction makes the temperature rise suddenly, so particular care is needed.

props.name: plant capacity 50 t/day
props.note: '50t/目' and '330目' are OCR readings of '50t/日' and '330日'
props.statement: Each section of the plant has a capacity of 50 t/day of refined methanol, 16,500 t/year at 330 operating days; coal-mine gas use including fuel is 1,500 m3 and power 1,400 kWh per t of methanol; construction began in spring Showa 33, was completed in October of the next year, and operation began that December.

props.name: reformed gas quenched to 300 °C
props.statement: The reformed gas is quenched to 300 °C on leaving the tubes to prevent the reverse reaction and the separation of carbon by CO decomposition.

props.name: steam reforming chosen; sulfur compounds almost absent
props.statement: Steam reforming was chosen over partial oxidation after weighing plant cost, power, fuel gas and steam prices, process-gas consumption and the use of nitrogen from an oxygen plant; the near absence of sulfur compounds also favoured it.

props.description: Electric heater at the top (start-up only); four catalyst baskets with a cooling coil at the outlet of each; below them one multitubular catalyst bed and at the bottom a multitubular heat exchanger. Feed enters at the bottom exchanger, is preheated, cools the multitubular bed through the tube walls, rises along the converter wall and enters the first bed from the top. Reaction heat is removed by natural circulation of water in the coils (50 kg/cm2 instead of 300 kg/cm2 in the former Fauser type); the steam heats a recovery boiler (10 kg/cm2) at the top; each coil has a control valve for the bed temperature.
